verdicts.correction: The runner classifies failure text: a hard limit re-picks a lane ONLY when it was launched with -A (bin/subfleet-claude:885; MAX_RETRIES=2 at :107, so up to 2 re-picks) and restarts the task under a fresh session id (:778); a pinned -a lane exits 4 with no re-pick, and `subfleet run` passes -A only on detached, unpinned dispatches (delegate.py:1358-1359). Transient errors back off on the same lane; an auth-failure signature exits 5 only if the lane token does not still authenticate, otherwise it is retried as transient (:868-878). Every exit snapshots a dirty worktree to refs/{claude,codex}-salvage/* without touching HEAD or the index — and, when -b was given, the same salvage function force-pushes to that remote branch (:367-371).

The hook parses only .tool_input.command (bin/subfleet-hook:42) and reads no agent identity — confirmed. It blocks `subfleet codex`/`subfleet claude`, `codex-run`/`claude-lane`/`subfleet-codex`/`subfleet-claude` and `codex exec|e|review` only in command position (47-59), and exempts any command whose text contains `SUBFLEET_ATTACHED_OK=1` (46) or, for the subfleet runners, a bare `-d` token anywhere (62-67). `subfleet run` with any flags passes because it never matches the prefilter or the offender test (tests/test_hooks.py:124-125). verdicts.correction: Not every notice is written to notices/<session>.jsonl and transcript/hook are not the only confirmations: when a live `--attach` inline waiter owns the run, on_finish returns a notice marked surfaced at finish time with surfaced_by 'inline-waiter' and never pushes it or calls append_notice (notify.py:978-988). Suggested wording: '...so a pushed notice is also written to notices/<session>.jsonl and confirmed only by transcript evidence or a hook render; a run whose inline --attach waiter is still alive is reported by that waiter instead and gets no push and no notice file.' Everything else in the cell checks out: session-id addressing at finish time (notify.py:183-217, 962-989), no acknowledgement read (notify.py:357-383, 403-404), 300 s grace and one re-push then LOST (tickle.py:1388-1392, 1500-1544), a one-shot `claude -p --resume` host only for a bypassPermissions session (tickle.py:1583-1606, 1291-1300), Telegram for dead sessions with pending work (liveness.py:159-247, 310-311).

meta.json fields and the per-attempt decisions.jsonl line are accurate (run_ledger.py:271-304, 509-572; delegate.py:289-293, 1021-1054, with a line also written for attempts refused before dispatch, delegate.py:1105,1116). The retention clause needs a qualifier: the 500-run / 2 GiB caps trigger pruning, but only finished (or meta-less) entries are removable — _prunable refuses any entry with finished_at None (run_ledger.py:614-617) — so unfinished entries never age out and the directory can exceed both caps.

The mechanism parts hold: delivery means the socket accepted the bytes (notify.py:403-404, 433-440), and the confirm / re-push / lost / revive / Telegram layers rest on the session registry, the peer-token key file, the socket protocol, the envelope and transcript field names (notify.py:8-18, 258-274; lanes.py:61-69). The 2.1.263 note over-attributes: lanes.py:36-46 records that the desktop app 'now' tags typed prompts promptSource: sdk and that the 172 affected desktop sessions were running Claude Code 2.1.263 — it does not establish which release introduced the change. Suggested wording: 'A Claude Code behaviour change, measured 2026-09-07 on 2.1.263, already broke lane detection once (lanes.py:36-47).' (Also note the code cites lanes.py:36-46; line 47 is the closing quote.)

`subfleet kill` defaults to a 10-second grace (cli.py:1540) and then SIGKILLs the run's process tree — the whole process group only when the runner pid leads its own group (detached launches use start_new_session), otherwise just that pid (run_ledger.py:935-946) — while README.md:26,77 and the cli module docstring (cli.py:18) describe SIGTERM only. Note the --grace help text at cli.py:1541 does mention the SIGKILL escalation.

extra_findings: Lines 104-105 ('the 500-run cap makes this a sample of 2026-09-11 to 09-17') inherit the pruning exception: unfinished entries are never pruned (run_ledger.py:614-617), so the ledger directory can hold more than 500 entries and the 7 orphans cited at line 159 sit outside the stated six-day window. Line 89 ('Synchronous outside a session, detached inside one, delegate.py:765-789') is accurate for `subfleet run` only; `subfleet resume-codex` is synchronous everywhere (resume_codex.py:204), which is worth stating since the same row lists resume among subfleet's durability story at line 80.

verdicts.correction: The active desktop login does not sort last unconditionally: in delegate._capacity_candidates the fable_stranded key precedes the active key (delegate.py:597-607), so for a non-Fable model a Fable-exhausted desktop login ranks ahead of every non-stranded lane; within the score it is only a 10-point handicap (delegate.py:568-574). The reserve clause should read: the default policy (cap_ratio 2.0, min_slack 0.05) is overridable by reserve-policy.json (reserve.py:58-86); an account whose usage payload carries no Fable window passes with no slack test, and an unmeasured account is withheld (reserve.py:180-188, 380-382). The OAuth token is injected at bin/subfleet-claude:826; 500-508 is the keychain fetch and 813-814 only unsets the API keys.

The peer's cwd is a neutral temp dir, but for a PR gate the peer's --review-root is the caller's live checkout, exposed to the peer with --add-dir (consensus.py:1112-1117; bin/subfleet-claude:809); only the patch/snapshot copy is immutable. 'On another account' is not enforced anywhere in consensus.py: the peer runs on whatever lane the capacity rules pick, and the active desktop login is deprioritised, not excluded (delegate.py:591-607; capacity.py:1338-1341). The rest of the cell (exact fingerprint, pinned peer, separate process, read-only, fail-closed verdict parsing, merge recheck plus --match-head-commit) holds.

The three-way divergence is real, but two details are off: delegate._capacity_candidates does not sort the login last outright — the active flag is the second sort key, behind fable_stranded (delegate.py:597-607) — and it also applies the same 10-point INTERACTIVE_HANDICAP inside the score (delegate.py:568-574). capacity._best_dispatchable is not a dispatch picker; it is the 'best lane' helper behind family_summaries (capacity.py:1376-1382), while cli 'pick claude' (cli.py:326,357-367) is the ranker the Claude runner actually shells out to.

extra_findings: Failure-handling row (line 88): 'Every exit snapshots a dirty worktree to refs/{claude,codex}-salvage/*' overstates it — the EXIT trap runs salvage only when cleanup_owned_prompt succeeds; if the owned prompt cannot be removed the run exits with a warning and no salvage or push (bin/subfleet-claude:437-446, 337-372).

Concurrency row precision caveat (the dispatch claim itself holds): in_flight is not display-only for Codex everywhere — reset_policy uses it as a tiebreak when ordering Codex homes for reset redemption (subfleet/reset_policy.py:130-152). Consider scoping the wording to dispatch ranking.

Caveat for whoever writes up D3f in the PENDING defects section: there is no gate list/status/abort subcommand, but `subfleet gate continue <id> --dry-run` returns the gate's effective state without --main-approve and without dispatching a peer (subfleet/consensus.py:1362-1470; tests/test_consensus.py:781-809), so a per-gate read surface does exist.

verdicts.correction: For ordinary jobs the deliverable is free text at deliverable.md (the daemon only checks it is non-empty when rc is 0) and submit accepts no result-schema field. One exception exists: a gate-review round's deliverable must be a sentinel-delimited JSON verdict object, validated field by field against a hand-written schema (schema_version 1, verdict enum, typed findings/notes/summary) in subfleet/gate/verdict.py, invoked on the peer deliverable at subfleet/gate/service.py:377-380. No JSON Schema library is used anywhere in the package.

extra_findings: WaitReason.APPROVAL (subfleet/contracts.py:40) is in the same state as DEPENDENCY: no code in the package ever writes wait_reason 'approval'. It is only read, at subfleet/daemon.py:1395, where it keeps a job out of admission. A document that lists approval waits as a working v2 mechanism is wrong for the same reason item V2-6 flags dependency waits.

The per-lane in-flight bound is not a flat 2. subfleet/scheduler.py:207-210 drops the cap to min(max_in_flight_per_lane, max_in_flight_unmeasured, 1), i.e. 1, for any lane with no fresh 'provider' reading inside reading_ttl_s (120 s, subfleet/default_policy.json:98-100). Stating '2 in flight per lane' without that qualifier overstates steady-state fleet concurrency.

Idempotency (item V2-2) is on the hashed payload, not the whole submission. subfleet/ids.py:54-62 and subfleet/daemon.py:551-556 hash prompt, workdir, workdir_head, task, tier, pinned_model, pinned_lane, sandbox, exclusions, out_path, allow_desktop, policy_hash, isolated_review, review_root and round_lease; kind, max_attempts, max_wall_s, parent_job_id, caller_session and name are excluded. A replay of one request_id that differs only in those fields returns the original job with created=False rather than the 'different payload' error at subfleet/daemon.py:561-562.

Automatic re-routing (item V2-3) is conditional, and a product document should not describe it as unconditional: a LIMITED outcome does not retry at all when the job has a pinned_lane, a TRANSIENT outcome does not retry when the job is pinned and has already spent a transient on that lane (subfleet/daemon.py:1992-1995), every retry is bounded by max_attempts (default 3, subfleet/default_policy.json:102), and only read-only jobs retry after a lost attempt.

caps.max_tokens_observed is a policy key that nothing enforces. subfleet/policy.py:180-182 validates it and subfleet/default_policy.json:104 sets it to null, but no module reads it to bound or stop a run; this is the policy-level counterpart of the per-job dead field in item V2-11.

readme_contradictions: consensus.py module docstring says the gate asks 'a pinned Fable or Sol peer' (consensus.py:5), but sol is retired and remapped to astra at gate creation (consensus.py:1276-1284; PEERS at :36). The README (README.md:843-844) is correct; the docstring is stale.

README.md:925-926 says 'Each round reserves a unique attempt directory under a lock.' In code the round entry, attempt_id and directory PATH are reserved under the flock (consensus.py:1006-1076), but the directory itself is created after the lock is released (consensus.py:1083 `_private_dir(round_dir)`). Uniqueness comes from the uuid token in the name, not from creating it under the lock.

README.md:879 says 'each completed review attempt records its dispatch arguments'; the code records peer_argv for every finished round including blocked/failed dispatches (consensus.py:1183-1192; test_consensus.py:135-136) - broader than 'completed', not a conflict.

README.md:898-901 lists 'missing positive Fable model attestation' as fail-closed; code confirms this applies ONLY to fable peers (consensus.py:1166-1169). README line 880-881 ('The model pin, revision approval, and model attestation checks remain required') could be read as covering astra peers; no attestation check exists for astra in consensus.py.

README:880-881 says 'The model pin, revision approval, and model attestation checks remain required', but `consensus.py:1164-1169` enforces the downgrade marker and served-model attestation only when `state['peer'] == 'fable'`; an astra/Codex peer completes a gate with no served-model attestation.

README:843-844 says 'A Fable main normally picks an Astra peer, and an Astra main picks a Fable peer'. The code has no complementarity or cross-provider requirement: `_new_gate` only checks membership in {fable, sol, astra} (consensus.py:1274-1275), so a Fable main can gate itself with `--peer fable`, and nothing prevents the peer landing on the same Claude account unless the caller passes `-x`.

README:913-915 says peers run 'with an immutable artifact copy and source access for PRs' and that project instructions are disabled; the immutability applies to the diff/snapshot only — for PR gates the peer's `--review-root` is the live, mutable checkout at `state['workdir']` (consensus.py:1112), and its freshness is guaranteed by the pre/post `_verify_pr_workspace` re-checks rather than by a copy or a dedicated worktree.

README:923-925 lists gate state contents as 'prompts, peer outputs, verdicts, main responses...'; the peer's output file does live under the round dir, but the prompt archived there is the pre-delegate text — the peer actually reads a private merged temp prompt with PREAMBLE_AUDIT prepended (delegate.py:1121-1133), which the README does not mention.
